claims.text: High configurational entropy in refractory HEAs induces severe local lattice distortions.
Severe local lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances the high-temperature strength of refractory HEAs.
Local lattice distortions generate an anomalous thermoelastic response by modifying thermal expansion at high temperature.
The initial as-cast refractory HEA has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The initial as-cast refractory HEA has a typical equiaxed grain structure.
A conventional refractory alloy with fewer principal elements has lower configurational entropy than the HEA.
A heat treatment can relieve local lattice distortions in the refractory HEA.
Local lattice distortion produces heterogeneous variations in atomic spacing.
Diffraction peak broadening provides evidence of local lattice-strain heterogeneity.
Local lattice distortions create internal stress fields.
Distortion-induced internal stress fields pin dislocations.
Local lattice distortions modify the elastic response of the HEA.
Between 1000°C and 1200°C, the HEA will have significantly higher yield strength than the conventional refractory-alloy baseline.
Between 1000°C and 1200°C, the HEA will have a reduced or nonlinear coefficient of thermal expansion relative to the baseline.
The HEA will exhibit broader diffraction peaks than the conventional refractory-alloy baseline.
Using an inert atmosphere or vacuum minimizes oxidation during high-temperature testing.
The proposed interpretation applies only while the alloy remains in the same phase and dynamic recrystallization or other high-temperature instabilities do not occur.
